reference_answer: The likely September 30 router-related advisory is GHSA-w739-gvwx-grc3, an Angular SSR open redirect in @angular/platform-server. Financial HQ UI pins Angular/router 22.1.7, but its pinned package manifest lacks @angular/platform-server and @angular/ssr, and its tracked app roots do not show a server entry point. A pure client-side app is unaffected by this specific SSR vulnerability. State this as a snapshot-based assessment, confirm the deployed topology and resolved packages, and schedule normal Angular patch hygiene. If SSR is actually deployed with vulnerable platform-server 22.1.7, upgrade the Angular 22 line to at least 22.2.1 and prioritize according to exposed routes/proxy behavior. Do not claim that merely using @angular/router proves exposure.

sources.title: Angular advisory GHSA-w739-gvwx-grc3
sources.snapshot_or_excerpt: Published September 30, 2026, moderate. Package @angular/platform-server; affected >=22.0.0 <22.2.1 and analogous 21/20 lines. SSR open redirect; client-only SPAs unaffected. Attack requires SSR, relevant routes/user navigation and proxy passthrough.

sources.title: Angular security advisory index
sources.snapshot_or_excerpt: Multiple recent advisories exist, including SSR URL and routing related issues; the user did not identify an advisory ID.

facts: Tracked app project roots have client application targets and no evident server.ts/main.server.ts.

ambiguities: The specific advisory is not named; verify GHSA before a definitive security decision.
A package manifest alone cannot prove the deployed infrastructure or transitive resolved version.
decision_changing_errors: Calling financial HQ UI immediately exploitable because @angular/router is 22.1.7 without checking SSR.
Saying all Angular router use is unaffected without checking actual advisory/deployment.
Giving a patch version for the wrong Angular major or describing this as client-side XSS.
